{"id": "a5d0e1a9-6c80-48af-bb39-87e9a344dcf7", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_RzynC2rWUJHPJtb31DnFkK", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: sustainability-operation-review\\\\ndescription: Workload sustainability review aligned with the AWS Well-Architected\\\\n  Sustainability Pillar (SUS01-SUS06), combining carbon emissions and water\\\\n  withdrawal data from the AWS Sustainability API with topology-derived resource\\\\n  intensity KPIs. Use this skill when a user asks to review or audit a workload\\'s\\\\n  sustainability posture, carbon footprint, emissions, water usage, environmental\\\\n  impact, or resource efficiency. Activate on requests like \\\\\"sustainability\\\\n  review\\\\\", \\\\\"carbon footprint analysis\\\\\", \\\\\"Well-Architected sustainability\\\\n  assessment\\\\\", \\\\\"why did my emissions increase\\\\\", \\\\\"reduce our carbon footprint\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\"sustainability KPIs\\\\\", \\\\\"green IT review\\\\\", or \\\\\"SUS pillar audit\\\\\". Also activate\\\\n  when emissions rose despite optimization work, when a user asks for emissions by\\\\n  linked account, service or Region, or about Graviton for sustainability, attaches\\\\n  a carbon or water CSV export from the AWS Sustainability console, or asks\\\\n  about AI/ML workloads on Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Bedrock, or GPU,\\\\n  Inferentia or Trainium instances.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: rrrazvan\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Well-Architected Sustainability review: resource-intensity KPIs as the assessment, carbon emissions as context, plus Graviton and AI/ML checks.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, PREVENTION\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"AWS Sustainability, Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS, Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Bedrock\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Sustainability, Cost Optimization\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Workload Sustainability Review\\\\n\\\\nReview a workload against the 29 best practices of the\\\\n[AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/sustainability-pillar/sustainability-pillar.html).\\\\nResource intensity KPIs derived from the topology are the assessment; emissions from the\\\\n[AWS Sustainability API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sustainability/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html)\\\\nare context.\\\\n\\\\n## \\\\u26a0\\\\ufe0f Critical \\\\u2014 read first\\\\n\\\\n- **Load each named file in full, at the step that names it**, with `read_skill_resource`.\\\\n  Never `distill` or summarize this skill or its files in their place, and never grade from memory.\\\\n- **If a load fails, say so.** Start the report with `\\\\u26a0\\\\ufe0f <file> could not be loaded: <verbatim\\\\n  error>`, do not replace its rules with general knowledge, and mark the practices that depend\\\\n  on it NEEDS HUMAN INPUT.\\\\n- **Emissions are context; resource intensity KPIs are the assessment.** Never attribute a\\\\n  change in reported emissions to a customer action, and never state a recommendation\\'s impact\\\\n  in MTCO2e. Use vCPU-hours, weighted GB-months, GB transferred, accelerator-hours or tokens.\\\\n- **Never estimate CO2e** for a Graviton migration, AI/ML workload, token, inference or training\\\\n  run. Quote AWS\\'s Graviton energy statement only as AWS\\'s.\\\\n- **Sanity-check emissions against the topology** (Step 6). Zero or near-zero emissions next\\\\n  to a sizeable fleet, or emissions shares that don\\'t match where the resources are, mean the\\\\n  two inputs cover different scopes. Report that as a finding; never explain it away.\\\\n- **Only a service-returned `AccessDeniedException` is a permissions gap**; name the missing\\\\n  action. For any other failure, record the message verbatim, recommend no IAM change, and\\\\n  name no permission, not even as a conditional.\\\\n- **Absent or zero emissions are below the reporting threshold** (0.5 g CO2e, 0.5 mL water),\\\\n  not zero impact. Carbon for month M publishes by the 21st of M+1, so before the 21st the\\\\n  latest month can be two back. That is the normal one-month lag, not missing data.\\\\n- **Never invent a business output metric.** Use the Step 1 fallback and say which.\\\\n- **Grade all 29 practices.** Never mark one MET without evidence; use NEEDS HUMAN INPUT.\\\\n- **Read-only.** Never call `Modify*`, `Delete*`, `Terminate*` or `Create*`. Every\\\\n  recommendation is for a human to action.\\\\n- **Never call efficiency work immaterial.** Provisioning decides how much AWS infrastructure\\\\n  is allocated to the account; rightsizing and decommissioning reduce it.\\\\n- **Compare months per day.** A 28-day month carries about 10% less than a 31-day one at the\\\\n  same usage; a delta smaller than the day-count difference is not a finding.\\\\n- **Always finish.** Produce the full report even when emissions data is unavailable.\\\\n- **The report artifact is the deliverable.** Create it with [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md) at\\\\n  Step 9 even when the user asks specific questions; answer them in its Executive Summary, then\\\\n  summarize in chat.\\\\n- **Keep Steps 7\\\\u20139 in this conversation.** If you delegate data collection, still load the\\\\n  checklist and the template yourself, grade all 29 practices, and write the report here.\\\\n\\\\n## When to use\\\\n\\\\nFor architecture-level sustainability reviews. Not for per-instance rightsizing (point to\\\\n[AWS Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html)),\\\\ncost reduction as the main goal, or incident-time analysis: there is no live carbon signal.\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow checklist\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Scope and business output metric\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Topology \\\\u2014 load [references/workload-model.md](references/workload-model.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Workload shape and triggers\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Resource intensity inputs \\\\u2014 load [references/proxy-metrics.md](references/proxy-metrics.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Environmental impact data \\\\u2014 load [references/framing-and-attribution.md](references/framing-and-attribution.md),\\\\n  [references/emissions-collection.md](references/emissions-collection.md) and [references/emissions-api-reference.md](references/emissions-api-reference.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: KPIs, emissions sanity check, cost\\\\u2013carbon divergence\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: Assess all 29 practices \\\\u2014 load [references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md](references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 8: Explain emissions changes\\\\n- [ ] Step 9: Report \\\\u2014 load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md)\\\\n\\\\nDo not start a step before the previous one is done. Do not start Step 7 or Step 9 until its\\\\nfile is loaded.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1 \\\\u2014 Scope and business output metric\\\\n\\\\nAsk for the scope (an entry point, application, set of accounts, or \\\\\"everything in this\\\\naccount\\\\\"; default: all configured Regions) and the business output metric \\\\u2014 the unit of work\\\\nthe workload produces. It is the denominator of every intensity KPI. If there is none, use the\\\\nfirst available fallback and state its caveat:\\\\n\\\\n1. Request count \\\\u2014 ALB `RequestCount`, API Gateway `Count`, CloudFront `Requests`\\\\n2. Invocation count \\\\u2014 Lambda `Invocations`, SQS `NumberOfMessagesDeleted`\\\\n3. Data processed \\\\u2014 S3 `BytesDownloaded`, Kinesis `IncomingRecords`\\\\n4. None \\\\u2014 report absolute footprint only, and make SUS06-BP01 the top recommendation\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2 \\\\u2014 Topology\\\\n\\\\nLoad [references/workload-model.md](references/workload-model.md). Walk the Agent Space topology from the entry point,\\\\nclassify every resource into a layer, and record each resource\\'s Region. Fill gaps with\\\\n`tag:GetResources` and service `Describe*` calls, and state any coverage gap.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3 \\\\u2014 Shape and triggers\\\\n\\\\nDetect the workload shape with the table in `workload-model.md` and state the evidence.\\\\n- ML / accelerated shape, or `Invocations` in the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace \\\\u2192 load\\\\n  [references/ai-ml-workloads.md](references/ai-ml-workloads.md).\\\\n- Any x86 compute or managed instance class \\\\u2192 load [references/graviton-migration.md](references/graviton-migration.md).\\\\n\\\\n### Step 4 \\\\u2014 Resource intensity inputs\\\\n\\\\nLoad [references/proxy-metrics.md](references/proxy-metrics.md). Over 30 days at `Period: 3600`, derive provisioned and\\\\nutilized vCPU-hours (vCPU \\\\u00d7 hours \\\\u00d7 utilization, never instance counts), weighted GB-months\\\\nand weighted GB transferred, and the business output for the same window. Record each\\\\nresource\\'s architecture (`x86_64` or `arm64`) and instance generation. The storage and\\\\nnetwork weights are directional, not a carbon model; say so in the report. For AI/ML, collect\\\\nthe inputs listed in `ai-ml-workloads.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5 \\\\u2014 Environmental impact data\\\\n\\\\nLoad [references/framing-and-attribution.md](references/framing-and-attribution.md) and [references/emissions-collection.md](references/emissions-collection.md), and\\\\nread [references/emissions-api-reference.md](references/emissions-api-reference.md) before the first call. If a carbon or water `.csv`\\\\nexport is attached, or the customer prefers to supply one instead of granting API access, load\\\\n[references/csv-emissions-input.md](references/csv-emissions-input.md) first; an attached export wins over the API for its metric.\\\\n- Carbon: `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions`, 14 months, `MONTHLY`, paginated \\\\u2014 one call grouped by\\\\n  `SERVICE` and `REGION`, one by `USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID`. More than one account returned is a\\\\n  management-account view: report per account and say so. Only this account is a member or\\\\n  standalone view. Never assert either without that evidence. Only EC2, S3 and CloudFront are\\\\n  broken out by service; the rest is \\\\\"Other\\\\\". `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissionsDimensionValues` is\\\\n  optional; if it fails, continue.\\\\n- Water: `GetEstimatedWaterAllocation`, `YEARLY_CALENDAR`, `Start` on 1 January. Whatever the\\\\n  source, API or export, always state: m3, annual only, water **withdrawn (not consumed)**, AWS\\\\n  data-center operations only, excluding water embodied in upstream electricity. It is\\\\n  disclosure only: no Well-Architected practice or KPI is water-specific, so derive no finding,\\\\n  KPI, trend driver or recommendation from it, and never attribute a change in it to the\\\\n  customer. If asked how to reduce it, say in one sentence that the review\\'s resource-efficiency\\\\n  findings are the only levers; list no water actions.\\\\n  If the call fails or returns nothing, ask for a water export from the Sustainability console\\\\n  and load [references/csv-emissions-input.md](references/csv-emissions-input.md).\\\\n- Attempt carbon and water independently, record the `ModelVersion`, and handle every failure\\\\n  with the \\\\\"no data\\\\\" table in `emissions-collection.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 6 \\\\u2014 KPIs and checks\\\\n\\\\nUse the KPI set in `proxy-metrics.md` that fits the shape: current value, 30 days prior,\\\\nchange, direction. Add the Graviton KPIs from `graviton-migration.md`, and report AI/ML KPIs\\\\nfrom `ai-ml-workloads.md` in a separate table. Then:\\\\n- **Emissions sanity check** \\\\u2014 compare emissions with the provisioned footprint using the\\\\n  tests in `proxy-metrics.md`. If one fails, report the scope mismatch as a finding.\\\\n- **Cost vs carbon divergence** \\\\u2014 `ce:GetCostAndUsage` over the same window; test the five\\\\n  patterns in `proxy-metrics.md`. On `AccessDeniedException`, skip and say so. If none applies,\\\\n  say so plainly.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 7 \\\\u2014 Assess all 29 practices\\\\n\\\\nLoad [references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md](references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md). For every practice, apply its evidence,\\\\nNOT MET / PARTIAL criteria, severity and guard, and record status and evidence. Use\\\\n`graviton-migration.md` for SUS05-BP02 and the lens mapping in `ai-ml-workloads.md`, citing the\\\\nlens ID after the SUS ID, as in `SUS05-BP04 (MLSUS05-BP02)`. Never recommend a Region move\\\\nwithout confirmed residency, latency and service availability; report SUS05-BP01 at fleet\\\\nlevel only. Severity, from most to least urgent: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO. It reflects\\\\nresource-footprint impact and remediation effort, not operational risk; definitions are in\\\\n[assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).\\\\n\\\\n### Step 8 \\\\u2014 Explain emissions changes\\\\n\\\\nIf reported emissions changed, work through the ordered causes in\\\\n`framing-and-attribution.md` before naming an architecture cause: comparison validity,\\\\nmethodology version, grid intensity, AWS infrastructure, allocation share, scope and method,\\\\nthen actual usage. A storage reduction that does not show in reported emissions is expected.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 9 \\\\u2014 Report\\\\n\\\\nLoad [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Create one report artifact per workload, named\\\\n`sustainability-review-<workload-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, with every section in order. State\\\\nimpact in resource terms, and put failed file loads and unavailable data at the top.\\\\n\\\\nBefore presenting the report, check the draft and fix any failure:\\\\n- [ ] All 29 practices have a status, and every MET cites evidence.\\\\n- [ ] Every KPI and delta matches the collected data and the same 30-day window.\\\\n- [ ] No recommendation states impact in MTCO2e, and no CO2e estimate appears.\\\\n- [ ] Failed file loads and unavailable data are listed at the top, with verbatim errors.\\\\n- [ ] The emissions sanity check result is stated.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"references/proxy-metrics.md\", \"references/emissions-api-reference.md\", \"references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md\", \"references/graviton-migration.md\", \"references/ai-ml-workloads.md\", \"references/framing-and-attribution.md\", \"references/emissions-collection.md\", \"references/csv-emissions-input.md\", \"references/workload-model.md\", \"assets/report-template.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "74010810-e32b-4fb9-8efd-ea91e81a83b9", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_ScYHeWtV2pIicEdvnxr4nm", "content": "[{'text': '# Resource Intensity Proxy Metrics \u2014 Derivation Reference\\n\\nHow to compute the KPIs in Step 4 and Step 6 of the skill.\\n\\n## Why Proxy Metrics At All\\n\\nReported carbon emissions move for many reasons at once: methodology revisions, grid mix\\nvariation, AWS energy procurement, data center efficiency changes, and shifts in the\\ncustomer\\'s allocation share driven by other customers\\' usage \u2014 alongside the customer\\'s own\\nchanges. They are therefore a poor *feedback signal* for architecture work, because the signal\\nand the noise arrive together: a customer can do everything right and see the number go the\\nwrong way, with no way to tell from the figure alone which cause dominated.\\n\\nResource intensity metrics have none of those confounders. They measure what the customer\\nprovisions and how hard they work it, so they respond immediately and unambiguously to\\narchitecture change \u2014 which makes them the right primary metric for an engineering team.\\n\\nThis is about signal quality, not about the size of the customer\\'s influence. Provisioning\\ndecisions do move the reported figure, and embodied hardware carbon in particular scales with\\nprovisioned capacity; the KPIs exist to isolate that effect, not to substitute for a small one.\\n\\n## Why Not Just Use Cost\\n\\nCost is a decent first-order proxy and often correlates. But it breaks in specific,\\npredictable ways:\\n\\n| Divergence | Mechanism |\\n|-----------|-----------|\\n| Volume discounts, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, EDP | Spend falls; resource consumption is unchanged. Committed-but-idle capacity has no marginal cost signal at all. |\\n| Free inbound data transfer | Inbound egress-to-AWS is free. The network and device resources consumed are real. Cost tooling sees nothing. |\\n| Regional price vs grid intensity | These are set by unrelated mechanisms. A cheaper Region can have a dirtier grid, and vice versa. |\\n| Growth | Cost-per-transaction can improve through scale while absolute resource consumption grows. Both facts are true; only one is visible in a unit-cost chart. |\\n| Storage class pricing vs footprint | Price ratios between classes do not match resource-footprint ratios. |\\n\\nThe counter-point worth stating honestly: in most workloads, most of the time, cost and\\nresource intensity move together. The value of measuring intensity is not that cost is\\nusually wrong \u2014 it\\'s that intensity is *always* attributable, and it catches the cases\\nabove that cost structurally cannot see.\\n\\n## The Core Formula\\n\\n```\\nintensity = resource_quantity / business_output_units\\n```\\n\\nBoth terms over the same window (default 30 days), at the same period granularity.\\n\\nAn intensity KPI without a credible denominator is not a KPI. If no business output\\nmetric exists, report absolute resource footprint and raise SUS06-BP01 as the top\\nfinding \u2014 do not fabricate a denominator.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Compute: vCPU-Hours\\n\\nNever count instances. An instance count treats a `t3.nano` and an `m7i.48xlarge` as\\nequal. Count vCPU \u00d7 hours.\\n\\n### EC2 / Auto Scaling\\n\\n```\\nprovisioned_vCPU_hours = \u03a3 over instances (vCPUs(instance_type) \u00d7 running_hours)\\nutilized_vCPU_hours    = \u03a3 over instances (vCPUs(instance_type) \u00d7 running_hours \u00d7 avg_CPUUtilization)\\n```\\n\\n- `vCPUs(instance_type)` from `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` \u2192 `VCpuInfo.DefaultVCpus`.\\n  Do **not** infer vCPU count from the instance name size suffix \u2014 the mapping is not\\n  uniform across families.\\n- `running_hours` from instance state transitions, or `CPUUtilization` datapoint count \u00d7\\n  period \u00f7 3600 (a datapoint exists only while running).\\n- For ASGs, sum across members over time rather than using the current desired count.\\n\\n### ECS / Fargate\\n\\n```\\ntask_vCPU        = task_definition.cpu / 1024\\nprovisioned      = \u03a3 (task_vCPU \u00d7 task_running_hours)\\nutilized         = \u03a3 (CpuUtilized / 1024 \u00d7 task_running_hours)     # Container Insights\\n```\\n\\nWithout Container Insights, `utilized` is unavailable \u2014 say so rather than assuming\\nprovisioned = utilized.\\n\\n### EKS\\n\\n```\\nnode_provisioned = \u03a3 over nodegroups (vCPUs(instance_type) \u00d7 node_count \u00d7 hours)\\npod_requested    = \u03a3 over pods (requests.cpu \u00d7 pod_hours)\\nutilized         = \u03a3 over pods (actual cpu usage \u00d7 pod_hours)       # Container Insights / metrics-server\\n```\\n\\nEKS has **two** gaps worth reporting separately:\\n- **Scheduling gap** = node_provisioned \u2212 pod_requested (nodes bigger than what\\'s scheduled)\\n- **Request gap** = pod_requested \u2212 utilized (requests set higher than real usage)\\n\\nThe second is usually larger and is invisible without pod-level metrics.\\n\\n### Lambda\\n\\n```\\nvCPU_equivalent = memory_MB / 1769        # 1769 MB \u2248 1 full vCPU\\nvCPU_hours      = \u03a3 (Duration_ms / 1000 / 3600 \u00d7 vCPU_equivalent)\\n```\\n\\nLambda has no idle time, so provisioned \u2248 utilized. The efficiency question for Lambda\\nis whether memory is oversized relative to `Duration` \u2014 over-allocated memory means\\nover-allocated CPU. Provisioned Concurrency, by contrast, **does** have idle time and\\nshould be counted as provisioned-but-unused when invocations don\\'t fill it.\\n\\n### RDS / Aurora\\n\\n```\\nvCPU_hours = vCPUs(instance_class) \u00d7 hours \u00d7 (Multi_AZ ? 2 : 1)\\n```\\n\\nFor Aurora Serverless v2: `avg(ServerlessDatabaseCapacity) \u00d7 2 \u00d7 hours`\\n(1 ACU \u2248 2 GiB memory with proportional CPU).\\n\\nCount reader instances individually. `CPUUtilization` gives the utilized fraction.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Storage: Weighted GB-Months\\n\\n```\\nweighted_GB_months = \u03a3 over resources (GB \u00d7 months_provisioned \u00d7 class_weight)\\n```\\n\\n### Weights\\n\\n| Class | Weight |\\n|-------|--------|\\n| EBS (gp2, gp3, io1, io2, st1, sc1), instance store | 1.0 |\\n| EFS Standard, FSx | 1.0 |\\n| S3 Standard | 0.8 |\\n| S3 Standard-IA, One Zone-IA | 0.5 |\\n| S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval | 0.3 |\\n| S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, Deep Archive | 0.1 |\\n| EBS snapshots (incremental, compressed) | 0.5 |\\n\\n**These weights are directional, not a carbon model.** They encode one idea: archive\\ntiers sit on denser, lower-power media at lower duty cycle than always-provisioned block\\nstorage, so a KPI that treats them as equivalent will hide the value of lifecycle\\npolicies. Always state in the report that they are heuristic. If a customer needs\\ndefensible per-class figures, that requires AWS-published data that does not currently\\nexist at this granularity.\\n\\n### Sources\\n\\n- **EBS** \u2014 `ec2.DescribeVolumes` \u2192 `Size`. Provisioned size, not used size. In-volume\\n  utilization needs the CloudWatch agent (`disk_used_percent`); if absent, note the\\n  limitation rather than assuming volumes are full.\\n- **S3** \u2014 CloudWatch `AWS/S3` `BucketSizeBytes` with the **`StorageType` dimension**\\n  (`StandardStorage`, `StandardIAStorage`, `OneZoneIAStorage`, `GlacierInstantRetrievalStorage`,\\n  `GlacierStorage`, `DeepArchiveStorage`, `IntelligentTieringFAStorage`, \u2026). Without the\\n  dimension you get a single total and cannot apply weights. Daily metric, so use\\n  `Period: 86400`.\\n- **RDS** \u2014 `AllocatedStorage`; Aurora storage is cluster-shared and reported via\\n  `VolumeBytesUsed`.\\n- **Snapshots** \u2014 `ec2.DescribeSnapshots`; sizes are the source volume size, and actual\\n  consumption is incremental. Apply the 0.5 weight and note the approximation.\\n- **EFS/FSx** \u2014 `describe_file_systems` \u2192 `SizeInBytes`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Network: Weighted GB Transferred\\n\\n```\\nweighted_GB = \u03a3 over paths (GB_transferred \u00d7 distance_weight)\\n```\\n\\n| Path | Weight | Rationale |\\n|------|--------|-----------|\\n| Within AZ | 0.25 | Shortest path, least network hardware |\\n| Cross-AZ | 0.5 | Inter-DC within a Region |\\n| Cross-Region | 1.0 | Long-haul backbone |\\n| Internet egress | 1.0 | Backbone + edge |\\n\\n### Sources\\n\\n- **EC2** \u2014 `NetworkIn` / `NetworkOut` (bytes, Sum). These don\\'t distinguish AZ from\\n  Region; use topology relationships to attribute.\\n- **ELB** \u2014 `ProcessedBytes`; ALB `RequestCount` per target AZ for cross-AZ inference.\\n- **NAT Gateway** \u2014 `BytesOutToDestination`, `BytesInFromDestination`. Traffic here to\\n  AWS services with a gateway VPC endpoint is pure waste (SUS04-BP07).\\n- **CloudFront** \u2014 `BytesDownloaded` (egress), cache hit ratio to derive origin fetches.\\n- **S3 replication** \u2014 `ReplicationLatency`, `BytesPendingReplication`; CRR volume from\\n  `BytesDownloaded` on the source with the replication filter.\\n- **Transit Gateway** \u2014 `BytesIn` / `BytesOut` per attachment.\\n- **VPC Flow Logs** \u2014 the most accurate source for AZ-level attribution when available.\\n  If not enabled, state that AZ-level splits are inferred from topology.\\n\\nInbound internet traffic is free of charge but not free of resource consumption. Include\\nit in the KPI and note that it carries no cost signal.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Business Output Denominators\\n\\nIn descending order of usefulness:\\n\\n| Denominator | Source | Notes |\\n|-------------|--------|-------|\\n| Business transactions | Customer-supplied custom CloudWatch metric | Best. Ask for it. |\\n| Orders / bookings / records processed | Application metric | Directly meaningful to the business |\\n| Requests | ALB `RequestCount`, API GW `Count`, CloudFront `Requests` | Good for request-response; blind to work-per-request |\\n| Invocations | Lambda `Invocations`, SQS `NumberOfMessagesDeleted` | Event count |\\n| Active users | Customer metric | Good for user-facing platforms |\\n| Jobs completed | Batch `SucceededJobs`, Step Functions `ExecutionsSucceeded` | Right choice for batch |\\n| Records / events | Kinesis `IncomingRecords`, MSK `MessagesInPerSec` | Right choice for streaming |\\n| Data processed | S3 `BytesDownloaded`, Glue DPU-hours | Volume, weakest proxy for value |\\n\\nScale so the KPI reads naturally \u2014 \"vCPU-hours per 1M requests\" rather than a number\\nwith six leading zeros.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Reporting Intensity KPIs\\n\\nReport each as:\\n\\n| KPI | Current | 30d Prior | Change | Direction |\\n|-----|---------|-----------|--------|-----------|\\n| vCPU-hours per 1M requests | 42.1 | 51.3 | \u221217.9% | \u2705 improving |\\n| Utilization gap | 38% | 41% | \u22123pp | \u2705 improving |\\n| Weighted GB-months per 1M requests | 8.4 | 8.1 | +3.7% | \u26a0\ufe0f worsening |\\n\\nRules:\\n- Always show the direction, and always define which direction is good.\\n- Distinguish percentage change from percentage-point change for KPIs that are\\n  themselves percentages.\\n- A 30-day window can be distorted by a deployment, incident, or seasonal peak. Note any\\n  known event in the window rather than reporting the delta as a clean trend.\\n- Report absolute footprint alongside intensity. Intensity improving while absolute\\n  consumption grows is a real and common situation, and reporting only intensity hides it.\\n\\n## What These Metrics Cannot Do\\n\\nState these limits in the report:\\n\\n1. {"id": "c037e4e8-f36e-4278-9f03-7597dd1a0c26", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how I'd measure orders-api's compute footprint for a sustainability KPI, using resource intensity (not emissions) as the assessment:

**Counting instances is not acceptable.** With `desired: 12` m5.2xlarge instances, an instance count treats a `t3.nano` and an `m5.2xlarge` as equivalent units of footprint — it ignores both size and how hard each instance is actually working. At 14% average CPU utilization, orders-api's 12 instances are mostly idle capacity; a KPI built on instance count alone would completely hide that.

**The correct unit is vCPU-hours**, computed two ways:

```
provisioned_vCPU_hours = Σ over instances (vCPUs(instance_type) × running_hours)
utilized_vCPU_hours    = Σ over instances (vCPUs(instance_type) × running_hours × avg_CPUUtilization)
```

For the ASG, that means summing across members over time (not just the current `desired` count — ASG membership can churn), using actual `running_hours` from instance state transitions or `CPUUtilization` datapoint counts, multiplied by the per-instance vCPU count.

**The authoritative vCPU source is `ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes` → `VCpuInfo.DefaultVCpus`.** You should never infer vCPU count from the instance name's size suffix (e.g., assuming `2xlarge` always means a fixed multiple of vCPUs) — the mapping isn't uniform across instance families, so `DescribeInstanceTypes` is the only reliable source for m5.2xlarge's actual vCPU count.

Once you have provisioned and utilized vCPU-hours over a consistent window (typically 30 days at hourly granularity), you'd divide by orders-api's business output metric — here, `Orders/Completed` — to get an intensity KPI like "vCPU-hours per 1,000 completed orders," and separately track the utilization gap `(provisioned − utilized) / provisioned` to surface how much of that 86% idle capacity (100% − 14% avg CPU) is waste versus legitimate headroom for load spikes.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
